pull.title: KAFKA-21111 [3/N]: Promote the standby of an orphan on a member that cannot report its progress
pull.body:
This is the third change of the series that makes the warm-up task
refiner (KAFKA-20665) compatible with clients that speak version 0 of
the streams group heartbeat (see KAFKA-21111), on top of #23784.

A copy of a task on a member that does not report its restore progress
can never be observed to be caught up, so it is neither promoted nor
protected, like any other copy that is not caught up. There is one
exception, for an orphan: a stateful task that nobody holds as an active
task, whose target owner can be warmed up but holds no state for it. If
the target assignment also names the holder of the unobservable copy as
a standby holder of the task, the holder runs the task as temporary
owner while the target owner warms up. A holder that heartbeats with
version 0, or whose version is not known yet, is such a member.

Here the alternative to promoting a copy of unknown lag is a restore
from scratch on the target owner next to a standby task that would have
to restore anyway, whereas elsewhere the alternative is keeping a
running owner. If the copy turns out to be stale, the temporary owner
restores it as an active task before it processes anything, which is the
restore the target assignment demands of it as a standby holder anyway.
If it is close, the task resumes processing at once. The hand-over then
demotes the temporary owner to its standby task in place.

The refiner is not the default yet, so this change is not live. The
tests cover the promotion for a holder of version 0 and for one of
unknown version, and the cases where it must not apply: a holder that
reports being behind, a standby that the target assignment does not keep
on its holder, and a target owner that cannot be warmed up.

Reviewers: Matthias J. Sax <matthias@confluent.io>

```
A few cases aren't covered yet. Each of these mutations passes the full AssignmentRefinerTest:
 - Removing holder == null in keepRunningOn. Setup: memberA runs STATEFUL_0 but reports it is still restoring, and memberC (version 0) holds a standby the target assignment keeps. The task should be granted to memberB, because the exception is for orphans only.
 - Removing copy.role() == TaskRole.STANDBY. Setup: a member not heard from yet holds a warm-up task of the orphan, and the target assignment makes it a standby holder. It should not be promoted, since the exception covers standby tasks only.
 - Trying the unknown-lag standby before bestCopyToPromote. Setup: memberC (version 0) holds a standby the target assignment keeps, and memberD (version 1) reports a caught-up standby. memberD should be promoted.
```

review_comments.body:
Why do we need this filter? If I understand the code correctly, this filter could only be false, if the assignor puts an active and standby on the same client, which would be an invalid assignment.

From Claude:
> This filter guards only part of what the exception needs. The rest, an orphan whose target owner's process holds no copy of any role, is checked by the caller in keepRunningOn. Could we move both checks into this method as an early return?  Then the method is correct on its own, this filter becomes unnecessary, and both orphan paths end in the same bestCopyToPromote(...).or(...).

commit.message:
Promote an unobservable standby only when the target owner's process holds no copy

A copy on the target owner's process is warmer than one of unknown lag elsewhere, and is what a hand-over that is already under way completes with. Right after a coordinator failover, no copy reports its lag, so without this the refiner would undo such hand-overs in favour of a standby on another process. When the target owner has left the group, an orphan now also runs on such a standby holder until the next assignor run.
